summary: Session stickiness reset under sudden traffic shift during canary weight adjustment
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary weight increase for rw-chat-7b-quant, a subset of Lexico Health's sessions experienced loss of session stickiness (version pin) and were routed to the canary model despite existing session pins. This caused mixed-model responses mid-session for ~120 users and several P1 customer alerts.

Impact:
- Approximately 120 active user sessions saw responses from a different model than pinned (mix of rw-instruct-13b-v1 and rw-chat-7b-quant).
- Some responses were semantically different, causing downstream validation failures for Lexico's medical QA workflow.
- Customer reported increased latency for affected sessions (median +180ms) and spurious rewriting of structured outputs.

Environment:
- Dedicated environment for Lexico Health, prod cluster: us-east, Dedicated pool #lexico-dedicated-3
- Canary rollout initiated via console at 2026-03-10T12:00:00Z (canary weight 10% -> 25% over 3min)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer creates a session and pins it to model version rw-instruct-13b-v1 via session.pin API.
2) Start steady traffic (50 rps) with long-lived sessions and KV cache usage.
3) Operator initiates canary weight adjustment for rw-chat-7b-quant from 10% to 25% over 3 minutes in us-east via Console -> Rollouts.
4) Observe routing logs for session IDs; some pinned sessions are routed to canary model within the 2-3 minute window.
logs:
Sample router trace (masked):
2026-03-10T12:01:22Z ROUTER select_route session_id=ab12cd pinned_model=rw-instruct-13b-v1 decision=CANARY weight=12% reason=weight-adjustment
2026-03-10T12:01:22Z SERVING start_inference model=rw-chat-7b-quant node=gpu-node-42 latency=210ms
2026-03-10T12:01:22Z SERVING kv_cache_miss session_id=ab12cd cache_version=42
-- stack traces and full router logs uploaded to customer staging S3 (link in investigation_notes)
investigation_notes: 12:25 - Support: Triage confirmed session-PIN mismatch pattern correlated with canary weight ramp window.
12:40 - Observed increased scheduling pressure on dedicated pool; autoscaler triggered a temporary allocation change in lexicod-pool-3.
13:05 - Routing metrics show route selection used fallback path when primary host set returned overloaded errors (503), fallback routing mistakenly ignored session pin header in that fast path.
13:20 - Initial hypothesis: under scheduler-induced host churn during the weight ramp, a fast fallback route bypassed session-affinity checks for latency reasons.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10T12:35: Customer reports mixed-model responses. Collected sample session IDs and trace logs. Escalating to SRE and Serving runtime owners.
Carlos Mendez (SRE) 2026-03-10T12:50: Looking at allocator events — a spot eviction in node group caused a short-term rebalancing window at 12:00-12:04. Possible link to route fallback.

Priya Shah (Serving Runtime) 2026-03-10T13:10: We found a fast-path in the routing-layer code that, on serve_host unavailability, calls select_fallback(host_group) and returns without evaluating session-pin cookie for performance. Reproduced locally under simulated host churn.
Lexico Health (Customer) 2026-03-10T13:30: This is blocking production validation. Can you provide immediate mitigation?

Support 2026-03-10T13:35: Applied temporary mitigation: paused canary weight ramp at 12% and forced session-affinity enforcement in routing config for lexicod-pool-3. Asking SRE for full rollback plan.
resolution: In Progress - temporary mitigation enforced: canary ramp paused and routing fast-path patched in configuration to re-check session_pin headers on fallback. Engineering to ship a code fix (PR-5123) to make session-affinity checks mandatory across all fallback paths and add unit + integration tests for host-churn scenarios. Postmortem scheduled and permanent guard added to rollout orchestration to delay weight increase when dedicated pool is in rebalancing state.
next_steps: 1) Merge and deploy PR-5123 to routing-layer in canary and run integration tests against simulated host churn. 2) Add a rollout pre-check to the Console to detect allocator rebalancing events and prevent weight changes while rebalancing is in-flight. 3) Deliver postmortem to Lexico Health by 2026-03-16 and include recommended client-side safeguards. 4) Add an automated smoke test that verifies session pins during incremental rollout.
